correctness.rationale: The base and A2 singular-curve blowups are Galois-stable and crepant by the rational equations and Burek Lemma 6.2. Each Q(i) section graph and conjugate is an honest Weil divisor. The finite, exhaustive Gaussian-rational certificate verifies the equation for every section, the 24 distinct discriminant roots and 96 nodes, all incidence tests, ruling signs via tangent-plane intersection determinants (with all pairwise consistency checks), and the 64/32 nonzero absolute local-class histogram. The completed conifold local class group is Z and the graded algebra for a nonzero local class is a Veronese of the primitive small-resolution algebra. The resulting relative Proj is a smooth projective small crepant resolution over Q; flatness and geometric MW rank follow from source propositions. Finite data alone would not prove the Proj result, so the local argument is supplied.

value.rationale: Arithmetic descent of projective small resolutions is not automatic: the two rulings at ordinary nodes may be exchanged by Galois, and global projectivity additionally requires an ample divisor. The displayed natural twelve-graph norm gives an effective rational Weil divisor whose class is nonzero at all 96 points, resolving precisely those arithmetic and global obstacles in a geometrically rank-twelve elliptic Calabi–Yau construction. Its 64/32 class distribution has concrete local-geometric meaning, not an arbitrary statistic. The arithmetic Mordell–Weil rank over Q is explicitly left open.
